latest_posts.caption: School is about to be in session! Join our exclusive Zero Click Summer School, two sessions on how to win in a world that no longer wants to send you clicks. Preorder the Zero Click Marketing book, and you can save your seat at the webinars.

Zero Click Marketing… THE BOOK.

It’s a thing. It’s almost done. And it’s now available for pre-order.

Brands and their websites are starving for traffic. Yet most marketing teams are still marketing like it’s 2018. If you’re struggling to explain why “just post the link on social” doesn’t work anymore, we see you.

Rand Fishkin and I wrote the book for you.

Zero Click Marketing is the honest, tactical, occasionally unhinged, and aggressively footnoted guide to earning attention, building an audience, and growing a business on a web that has mostly stopped sending clicks.

👎 More than half of Google searches now end without a click.
👎 Social platforms punish links.
👎 AI tools are answering the questions that used to land on your site.
👎 And your boss still wants a last-click attribution report by Friday.

This is not a bunch of blog posts in a trench coat. It’s the playbook Rand and I have been running ourselves since I coined the phrase in 2022, and Rand started building on it with his research into how the web is changing.

Pre-orders are live now. The book comes out this fall.

Pre-orders help our publisher convince bookstores to carry the book, determine the print run, and get this thing into the hands of more marketers who are trying to figure out what the hell is happening to traffic, attribution, and modern marketing.

Plus, pre-order readers get access to Zero-Click Summer School, a live online workshop series Rand and I are teaching this summer.

Clicks are dying. But marketing is just getting interesting.

Preorder at zeroclickmarketing.co/book

B2B swag is forgettable. But not this. Wunderkind sent a World Cup kit where each “player card” is a shopper your brand already has — and usually loses. 7 personas, 7 missed-revenue moments: the messy cross-device journey, the almost-buyer who just needed the right nudge at the right time, the early visitor who isn’t ready to buy but truly wants to learn more.

A lot of “lost” conversions aren’t a traffic problem. They’re a recognition and timing problem. 

Which of the 7 is costing you the most?

Our friend Amanda Natividad—marketer, food person, soon-to-be-published author, all-around amazing human—is speaking at MarketingProfs B2B Forum this fall. To promote her FIRST TIME EVER appearance there, she made a bread-pun video.

7 years ago I was 4 months postpartum and newly laid off. Had no idea what I was going to do next, and was having regular nightmares about failing my family and my career. Last week, I gave the closing keynote at the Turing X SYSTM Growth Summit in front of 300+ people. 

Never in my wildest dreams did I ever think this could happen. I’m infinitely grateful to everyone who has ever taken a chance on me, supported me, and put up with my corny jokes and silly slide decks.
